pattern.crimePattern: husband smothers the hotelier wife who was divorcing him and removing him from her company, during the drumming at a bush dinner, and carries her home "asleep"
pattern.notes: Fictional camp, hotel group and family. The Maasai performers are the camp's pride and are thanked by name in the reconstruction; they are not background noise. No method detail beyond "a dinner-chair cushion".

ob.text: A luxury tented camp reports a guest, Laila Bajaber (44), hotel owner from Mombasa, found dead in her bed in tent 7 by the morning tea service at 06:15. Suspected death in her sleep.

facts.text: Laila Bajaber was found dead in her bed in tent 7 by the morning tea service at 06:15. Suspected death in her sleep.
Tent 7: Laila under the covers; her slippers by the bed are clean; the soles of her feet carry red soil. The camp paths are grey gravel; the fig-tree site is red soil.
Bush-loo tent at the dinner site: a diamond stud earring on the floor mat; scuffed sand inside the doorway.
Bush-dinner inventory: fourteen chair cushions sent out; thirteen returned.
Kakuta: "Madam slept on his shoulder the whole drive. We hit the big bump at the lugga crossing hard. She didn't move at all. I remember thinking, she sleeps like the dead."
Kakuta was at the vehicle through the drumming; he is in guests' photos at 21:40.
Lemanken: "Mr Faisal waved me away at the vehicle. He said, 'My wife is asleep, I'll carry her.' I walked behind with the torch to the tent door." That was at 22:25.
Lemanken was at the camp vehicle bay all evening until the vehicle returned at 22:22.
Guests' photos: Laila at the table at 21:30. In the drumming, 21:35–21:45, her chair is empty, and Faisal's is empty from 21:37 to 21:44. At 21:50 he is back; hers is still empty.
One frame at 21:41: in the lantern light, a man in a white linen shirt walks towards the loo tent with a dinner cushion under his arm. It is Faisal.
Guests' photos: Mwanakombo at the table through the whole drumming.
Laila's email from her lawyer, Monday: "Petition filed. Board meeting Friday: resolution to remove F. Bajaber as director."
Laila's email: no rival bid for any of her hotels.
Manager's radio log: Sylvester was at camp all evening; his calls are logged from 19:10 to 23:40.
Salma: the anniversary gift was Laila's to him, a watch, and he liked it.
Salma: all of Laila's jewellery is accounted for, except one diamond stud earring.
Mwanakombo: "She fired me every month. She always rehired me."
In Faisal's suitcase: a dinner-chair cushion with the camp's embroidered logo, a lipstick smear on one face.
Autopsy: smothering. Burst blood vessels in the eyes; fibres in the airway.
Autopsy: lividity in the buttocks and legs as well as the back. She sat upright for a while after death, then lay flat.
Autopsy: death between 21:30 and 22:00.
Autopsy: no sign of asthma or allergy.
Lab: the fibres in Laila's airway match the cushion from Faisal's suitcase.
Toxicology: a little wine; nothing else.
Faisal: "She was alive in the vehicle. She walked into our tent, went to bed at half past ten, and I read until midnight."
Faisal: "She was tired. I carried her. She was asleep."
Sylvester: "Every guest was escorted to their tent and walked in on their own feet."
Sylvester: he didn't check. "If the conservancy hears guests walk around without escort, we lose our licence."
Mwanakombo: "I was at the table the whole time."

interrogations.intro: Faisal sits on the veranda of tent 7 with his head in his hands. "She was alive in the vehicle. She walked into our tent. She went to bed at half past ten and I read until midnight."

topics.reply: The divorce? A misunderstanding. We would have sorted it out. We always did.

interrogations.intro: Sylvester has his radio in his hand and a guest list on a clipboard. "Every guest was escorted to their tent and walked in on their own feet."
Mwanakombo is packing her own bag. "She fired me yesterday. I'm going home."

topics.reply: Look at the photos; I'm in all of them. She fired me every month. She always rehired me.

interrogations.intro: Kakuta leans on the game vehicle's bonnet. "I drove them back. I'll tell you about the bump."
Lemanken holds his torch in both hands. "Guests insist. He insisted."

contradictions.reaction: "I didn't check. If the conservancy hears guests walk around without escort, we lose our licence."
He lifts his head. "...She was tired. I carried her. She was asleep."
Faisal looks at the cushion in its bag for a long time. "Friday," he says. "She was going to read it out to the board on Friday." He asks for a lawyer.

proof.concludes: She didn't move at the lugga bump because she was already dead: she was smothered, and sat upright for a while after death before she lay flat.
She never walked into the tent: red soil on bare soles, clean slippers. Faisal waved the escort away and carried her; the manager's escort story was untrue.
During the drumming both their chairs were empty; at 21:41 Faisal walked to the loo tent with a cushion, and her earring is on its floor mat. She died there, between 21:37 and 21:44.
The fourteenth cushion is in his suitcase, with her airway's fibres on it.
She was divorcing him and removing him from her company on Friday. At the bush-loo tent, Faisal Bajaber smothered Laila with a dinner-chair cushion during the drumming.

reconstruction.text: On Monday Laila files for divorce in Mombasa and, as majority owner, calls a board meeting to remove Faisal as a director. She tells him at lunch on Tuesday.
Tuesday night, the bush dinner under the fig tree. At 21:35 the drummers from the conservancy, led by Parsapaet ole Kaelo, begin ten minutes of drumming and song that hold every guest.
Laila walks to the loo tent in the dark. At 21:37 Faisal follows with the cushion from his chair, and smothers her inside the tent.

He sits her on a camp chair outside in the dark and comes back to the table: "She's resting, she has a headache." At 22:10 he carries her to the vehicle, "asleep", her head on his shoulder. At the lugga bump she doesn't move.
At camp he waves the escort away, lays her in bed, sets her slippers neatly by the bed and packs the cushion. Kakuta, who notices everything, remembers thinking: she sleeps like the dead.

clockPlan.note: One warrant on his luggage. Detain Faisal before the 11:00 flight; the fibre result comes back in 12 h, inside the 24.

ui.beatNotes: A witness's throwaway remark as evidence. The guide's line about the bump can be dragged into the notebook as a fact; it's the only way to the twist. The notebook teaches players to pin sentences, not just objects.
